*Any resemblance with a fictional character is purely accidental.

The challenge we chose was: “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions”. H.A.L. 9001 is a tool that allows astronauts and medicine professionals to quickly analyse, interpret and organize the data gathered by the multiple sensors incorporated in their suits and spaceship, by doing the following:

1. Providing an intuitive and efficient visual interface. 
2. Sending and receiving data from and to the earth base.
3. Detecting and alerting of health emergencies.
4. Showing the astronauts only the information that's useful enough to them.
5. Arranging and preprocessing the data in order to make it easier and faster to interpret by the medical team on earth.
details:
Detailed Project description:

General functionality

H.A.L. 9001 is a software that accesses a database which contains the results of the measurements of several sensors, performs an analysis and displays the results in an organized graphic interface. 

To delimit this project, our team made certain assumptions:

  1. There exists a scheduler for each astronaut in which their tasks are displayed organized by priority and urgency. The health tasks are included in this system. 
  2. There is a local database in which the data gathered by the multiple sensors is collected, each sensor sends information to this database, not necessarily at the same rate. We did not create this database, we just have access to it.
  3. The sensors are already installed. We are just creating software, not modeling hardware.
  4. There is a medical team on earth that’s monitoring the data and assign health-related tasks to each member of the mission.
  5. Astronauts do not need to know the state of every variable, we need to give them enough information but not too much or they could get overwhelmed.

 Two versions

There is a version of this program designed for the medical team on earth and another for the astronauts. The purpose of this separation is to make a distinction on the information that is shown. This can help to avoid overwhelming the crew with large amounts of data which could also have negative effects on their psychological state. 

The graphic interface

H.A.L. 9001 has an interface divided into tabs: Live monitor, Crew overview, Communications and Manual input.

Live Monitor, 3D diagram:

It shows a 3D model in which, if a physiological system is presenting anomalies, it changes colour. It is also possible to click on each system to get more specialized information about it.

Live Monitor, Vitals:

Graphics with hearth rate, O2 saturation, and much more are displayed.

Figure 2

Sleep chart, shown in the vitals tab.

Crew overview:

Allows access to the information of all the astronauts, facilitating a holistic analysis.

Communications:

Provides a window between the medical team and the crew without the necessity of changing the application and optimizing times

Manual input:

If a sensor fails or there is a parameter that requires a description from the crew, it can be handled in this tab.

How it works

Pre-existing systems:

We have considered the following infrastructure: 

On Earth, there is a base which contains a communications system, a data base and a connection with the medical team. The medical team elaborates and sends health-related tasks to the crew to complete, based on the results of the measurements. On the other hand, in the spaceship there is a communications module, another database, and a set of sensors. 

Figure 3

[IMAGE ID NOT FOUND title:"" ]

A simplified overview of the systems and their interactions.

Data Analysis

Variables taken into consideration

Ambient:

  1. Cabin pressure, partial pressure of O₂, O₂ concentration, partial pressure of CO₂, CO₂ concentration, carbon monoxide (CO) concentration, volatile organic compounds (VOC) concentration, etc.

Astronauts:

Health Variables: reaction test, neuromotor test, heart rate, blood pressure, sleep quality, body composition, etc. 

Location Variables: where and how much time the astronaut is.

Holistic evaluation:

Besides contemplating the results of each crew member on its own,  H.A.L. 9001 provides functionalities to evaluate the group and the ambient as a whole, which can help to identify causes to common problems.

Data sent to Earth:

Earth receives a document with an organized layout displaying the values of all the variables. 

Limitations and Future improvements:

  1. Adding a gamification system.
  2. Creating different versions adapted to the environment (outer space, the moon, mars)
  3. Add voice input.
  4. H.A.L. 9001 does not contemplate the automatic activation and regulation of actuators in response to the measurements taken by the sensors. In a future version, a subsystem capable of that can be added.
  5. Several variables had been put aside in order to create a prototype. Those can be included in a future version.
